info.name: UnclogMe - GDO Online Reporting Bot API
info.description:
# GDO Online Reporting API

**Audience:** the integrator of the GDO Online Reporting RPA bot (Jonathan / "John").
**Status:** live on Prod, tested end-to-end. The bot polls on its own schedule (no endpoint to expose); only the rollout gates remain.
**Last updated:** 2026-07-23.

> This is both the **API reference** and the doc for the Postman collection in this folder. It
> documents the **current** contract of the two endpoints your bot talks to, plus the surrounding
> pieces (event push, status surfaces, evidence storage, error codes). Nothing here is a secret: key
> **values** are sent to you privately, never committed. This repo is public.

---

## 1. What this is

The bot files **GDO Online Reporting** on the Miami-Dade DERM portal. For us that is **Line Item 27**
on a client's job, so the **unit of work is a serviced VISIT** for one of the clients that carry that
add-on, not a manifest — but the queue is **deduped per dump**, so you never receive the same manifest
twice (see §3). When we service such a client and their DERM manifest is filed + linked to the
visit, that visit becomes a "please file the online report" job for the bot.

It is a **small, targeted feed** (only a few clients carry Line Item 27), **server-to-server**, and
**compliance-critical**: the design's first job is to *never double-file a report to the county*. All
the lifecycle rules below exist to guarantee that.

Two endpoints, both live:

| Direction | Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| bot → us | `GET`  | `/functions/v1/rpa-derm-queue`  | "What should I report?" |
| bot → us | `POST` | `/functions/v1/rpa-derm-result` | "Here is what happened." |

Base URL: `https://wbasvhvvismukaqdnouk.supabase.co`

---

## 2. Authentication

Every call carries the header **`x-rpa-key`** (value sent to you privately). There is **no Supabase
JWT** and no database connection: the key is the auth, checked inside each function.

- There is **one key** — the `x-rpa-key` you send us on every `GET`/`POST` above. It is matched
  against a **comma-separated** secret on our side, so we can rotate with zero downtime (add new,
  you switch, we remove old). You never see the list.
- The key lives only in your Railway environment variables, never in code or logs.

Missing/invalid key → `401 {"error":"unauthorized"}`. Key not configured on our side →
`503 {"error":"service_not_configured"}`.

---

## 3. `GET /functions/v1/rpa-derm-queue` — the work queue

Returns up to **25** reports to file, **oldest first**.

**Query params**

| Param | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `dryrun` | Serve a fixed set of **historical** visits for testing. Omit for the live queue. |

**Response `200`**

```jsonc
{
  "generated_at": "2026-07-21T15:00:00.000Z",
  "mode": "live",              // or "dryrun"
  "count": 3,
  "reports": [ { /* report object, see below */ } ]
}
```

**Report object** — every field the bot needs to file one report:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `visit_id` | integer | **The work key.** Echo it back on your result POST. |
| `manifest_id` | integer | The linked DERM manifest (context; optional to echo). |
| `dry_run` | boolean | `true` when this came from `?mode=dryrun`. |
| `client_code` | string | e.g. `041-MB`. |
| `client_name` | string | |
| `client_email` | string \| null | |
| `address`, `city`, `zip`, `county` | string | Service location. |
| `gdo_number` | string \| null | The GDO permit number. |
| `service_date` | date | When the visit was serviced. |
| `dump_ticket_date` | date | Date on the disposal receipt. |
| `white_manifest_number` | string \| null | Miami-Dade WWTP/dump receipt number. |
| `disposal_facility` | string \| null | |
| `documents.address` | string[] | **Signed URLs** to the DERM Address / Manifest Form sheet(s). |
| `documents.receipt` | string[] | **Signed URLs** to the Transporter Manifest / WWTP receipt(s). |

**Signed URLs are valid ~4 hours** and are minted fresh on every fetch. Download everything at the
start of a run; **never log or persist the URLs**.

### Queue lifecycle (why a visit does or does not appear)

- **One row per dump (DERM manifest).** A county report is filed per **dump ticket / manifest**, so the
  queue returns **one report per manifest** even when more than one visit fed that dump (represented by
  the visit whose service date is closest to the dump). `visit_id` is still your work key — you just
  never see the same dump twice in a batch.
- A dump stays in the live queue **until it is successfully reported** — so nothing is dropped if the
  bot is down for a while.
- It leaves the queue **permanently** once the county confirms it (a `SUCCESS` result with a
  `portal_confirmation`, section 4). This is **manifest-scoped**: reporting *any* visit of a dump clears
  the whole dump, so a sibling visit can never re-surface an already-filed report.
- After any attempt — or the moment we hand it to you — the dump is **held for 20 hours** (a dispense
  *lease*, also manifest-scoped) so a crash between filing and the result POST can never cause a
  re-dispense and a double-file.
- The live queue only contains visits with a `dump_ticket_date` on/after a **launch cutoff** (currently
  `2026-07-21`). This exists so the bot's first live run cannot re-submit the entire historical backlog
  to the county. We widen the cutoff deliberately if a backfill is ever wanted.
- `?mode=dryrun` serves already-serviced **historical** visits and does **not** place a lease; use it
  freely for testing.

---

## 4. `POST /functions/v1/rpa-derm-result` — record an outcome

Same `x-rpa-key`. **Idempotent on `(visit_id, run_id)`**: a retried POST returns `200 {deduped:true}`
and changes nothing (first write wins).

**Request body**

| Field | Type | Req | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visit_id` | integer | ✅ | From the queue. |
| `manifest_id` | integer | | Optional; echo it back if you have it. |
| `run_id` | string | ✅ | Charset `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, ≤100 chars. **Generate ONCE per report attempt, before you hit the portal, and reuse it verbatim on every retry.** It becomes part of the screenshot storage key. |
| `status` | string | ✅ | Short uppercase code, `^[A-Z0-9_]{1,64}$`. Use the literal **`SUCCESS`** for a confirmed report (see below). |
| `retryable` | boolean | ✅ | `true` for transient problems (portal timeout); `false` for data problems (missing field). |
| `failure_reason` | string | | ≤1000 chars. |
| `attempted_at` | string | ✅ | ISO 8601 UTC. **Log/audit only** — our queue timing uses our own server clock, so a skewed bot clock can never cause a double-file. |
| `portal_confirmation` | string | | ≤200 chars. Whatever number/text the portal returns. **Required for a real `SUCCESS`.** |
| `screenshot` | string | | base64 JPEG, ≤5 MB decoded. |
| `screenshot_missing_reason` | string | | ≤300 chars. **Provide this OR `screenshot`** — every result needs one. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | | Ignored / derived server-side; harmless to send. |

Unknown fields → `400 {"error":"unknown_field_<name>"}`.

**Two hard rules enforced on our side:**

1. **No optimistic success.** A visit only counts as reported (permanent queue exit) when
   `status = 'SUCCESS'` **and** a `portal_confirmation` is present. Any other confirmed status is fine
   too as long as you send `portal_confirmation`, but `SUCCESS` is the clean permanent-done signal.
2. **Evidence or a reason.** Every result carries a `screenshot` **or** an explicit
   `screenshot_missing_reason`. If a screenshot is oversized/undecodable we still **record the result**
   and just flag the missing evidence — we never drop a genuine attempt over a screenshot problem.

**Responses**

| Code | Body | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | `{"recorded":true,"deduped":false,"id":<n>}` | New result stored. |
| `200` | `{"recorded":true,"deduped":true,"id":<n>}` | Duplicate `(visit_id, run_id)`; no-op ack. |

**If you do not get a 2xx, keep the result locally and retry the same POST** (same `run_id`) until you
do. Never treat a report as done before we acknowledge it.

**Screenshots:** send the bytes in the POST; we store them in a **private** bucket (`rpa-evidence`,
client data) and record only the path. You never need storage credentials. If images ever exceed the
5 MB cap routinely we will switch you to a signed upload URL.

---

## 5. How you run it — you poll, on your own schedule

**You own the timing. There is no push from us** — you don't expose any endpoint, and there is no
second "run" key. Just poll the queue and file whatever it returns:

- Poll `GET /rpa-derm-queue` on a **slow schedule** (every 15–30 min is plenty), file each report,
  and POST the result. That's the whole loop.
- Reporting is safe to run as often as you like: the queue only hands you visits that still need
  filing (a `SUCCESS` permanently removes one), each dispensed visit is **leased for 20h** so a crash
  can't get it re-handed-out, and `rpa-derm-result` is **idempotent on `(visit_id, run_id)`** — so a
  duplicate or retried run never double-files.
- Nothing on our side calls you, so you never need an inbound endpoint or a public URL.

---

## 6. What the result feeds (status surfaces)

Your `POST` results drive per-visit "GDO report filed / pending / failed" chips in our apps:

- `derm.gdo_report_status` — per visit, shown in the internal DERM Tracker.
- `customer.gdo_reports` — per visit, shown on the customer's Field Portal.

Every write from the bot is attributed in our audit trail as `app_source = 'gdo-report-bot'`, and every
result is logged in `public.derm_portal_submissions` (visit_id / run_id / status / confirmation /
screenshot path / dry_run).

---

## 7. Error reference

All errors are `{"error":"<code>"}` with the HTTP status shown.

**Both endpoints**

| Status | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing/wrong `x-rpa-key`. |
| 405 | `method_not_allowed` | Wrong HTTP method. |
| 503 | `service_not_configured` | Key secret not set on our side (tell us). |

**`rpa-derm-queue`**

| Status | Code |
|---|---|
| 500 | `queue_query_failed` |

**`rpa-derm-result`**

| Status | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_json` | Body was not JSON. |
| 400 | `unknown_field_<name>` | A field we do not accept. |
| 400 | `visit_id_required_integer` | Missing/invalid `visit_id`. |
| 400 | `manifest_id_must_be_integer_or_omitted` | Bad `manifest_id`. |
| 400 | `run_id_must_be_alnum_dot_dash_underscore_max100` | Bad `run_id` charset/length. |
| 400 | `status_must_be_short_uppercase_code` | `status` failed `^[A-Z0-9_]{1,64}$`. |
| 400 | `retryable_boolean_required` | `retryable` not a boolean. |
| 400 | `failure_reason_max_1000_chars` | Too long. |
| 400 | `portal_confirmation_max_200_chars` | Too long. |
| 400 | `attempted_at_must_be_iso8601` | Not a valid ISO timestamp. |
| 400 | `screenshot_missing_reason_max_300_chars` | Too long. |
| 400 | `screenshot_or_screenshot_missing_reason_required` | Neither provided. |
| 400 | `success_requires_portal_confirmation` | `SUCCESS` without a `portal_confirmation`. |
| 422 | `visit_not_found_or_deleted` | `visit_id` unknown or soft-deleted. |
| 500 | `visit_lookup_failed` / `result_store_failed_retry` | Transient; retry the same POST. |

---

## 8. Rollout gates

Nothing hits the county for real until, in order:

1. A **dry-run pass** over the historical visits (`?mode=dryrun`) — ~29 are available now.
2. The **first live report on a single visit** Fred picks, verified on the county side.
3. Then it **opens for all** the eligible clients.

---

## 9. Operating notes (our side)

- **Watchdog:** a daily health check surfaces a stuck queue / repeated data errors / storage failures /
  a code-27 visit whose service is not DERM-manifest-requiring (a mis-applied add-on to flag).
- **Launch cutoff:** currently `2026-07-21` bounds the live queue.
- **Evidence retention:** screenshots live in the private `rpa-evidence` bucket keyed `visit_id/run_id.jpg`.
- **PII note (under review):** the queue currently signs the **raw multi-client** address sheet. This is
  intended because county submission needs the real document, but if the portal only needs the client's
  own row we will serve the redacted copy instead — pending confirmation of what the portal requires.

---

## 10. Integration checklist (what we still need from you)

1. **The CSV column list** you read today, so we can flag any field name you expect that we do not
   already return.
2. Your **repo link** (we set up a private repo under the `webunclogmecom` org; Railway auto-deploys
   from `main`).

We send the key and the county portal login privately. You expose nothing to us — you poll (section 5).

---

## 11. Using this Postman collection

The collection in this folder (`gdo-reporting-bot.postman_collection.json`) is a ready-to-run test
harness for the two endpoints above.

**Setup (once):** right-click the collection **UnclogMe - GDO Online Reporting Bot API** → **Edit** →
**Variables** tab → paste your key into `rpaBotKey`'s **Current value** column → **Save**. The value is
`RPA_BOT_KEY` in `Supabase/.env` (never commit it). Auth is one collection-level header
`x-rpa-key: {{rpaBotKey}}`, so every request uses it automatically. (An optional
`UnclogMe - RPA (Prod)` environment is also included; if selected it overrides the collection value.)

**Run:** top to bottom. Start with **1. Queue → Queue - dry-run** — it returns real historical code-27
visits and captures the first `visit_id` into a collection variable the Result requests reuse. Then run
**2. Result** (all `dry_run:true`, so they record separately and never affect the live queue or what
customers/apps see), and **3. Validation** (shows the endpoint rejecting bad input).

**Variables:** you only ever set `rpaBotKey`. `baseUrl` is preset. `dryRunVisitId` / `dryRunManifestId`
are auto-captured into **collection** scope by the dry-run request — leave them empty and do **not** add
them to a selected environment (an empty environment copy shadows the captured value and blanks the
Result requests).

**Gotcha:** a `401 unauthorized` means `rpaBotKey` is still blank (or an empty environment is selected
and overriding it). Dry-run result writes create harmless `dry_run` rows in our log table; clear anytime
with `DELETE FROM public.derm_portal_submissions WHERE dry_run;`. There is deliberately no
"SUCCESS needs confirmation" test here: that rule (and the double-file guards) apply only to LIVE
reports, so a dry-run `SUCCESS` is exempt and cannot be exercised against dry-run data.

request.description:
Up to 25 REAL historical code-27 visits to report, keyed by visit_id, each with client + service fields, gdo_number, and 4h signed document URLs. Captures the first visit_id/manifest_id for the Result requests. Read-only.

--- 2026-08-11: ONE ROW PER (TICKET, PERMIT) ---
A client with N active GDO permits owes Miami-Dade N reports per qualifying dump ticket (we pump both traps). Each row now carries gdo_number for the permit THAT ROW IS FOR, plus a new gdo_id column.
The queue serves at most ONE permit per ticket per batch: the 20h manifest-grained lease holds the rest until the served one is filed. So a multi-permit ticket appears again on a later poll with its next permit, and a three-permit client files over about two days. Nothing about the 25-row cap changes.
You do NOT need to send the permit back. We resolve it server-side from the pair we served.

exec: const j = pm.response.json();
pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('mode = dryrun', () => pm.expect(j.mode).to.eql('dryrun'));
pm.test('reports is an array', () => pm.expect(j.reports).to.be.an('array'));
if (j.reports && j.reports.length) {
const r = j.reports[0];
pm.collectionVariables.set('dryRunVisitId', r.visit_id);
pm.collectionVariables.set('dryRunManifestId', r.manifest_id);
pm.test('report keyed by visit_id, has gdo + signed docs', () => {
pm.expect(r.visit_id, 'visit_id').to.be.a('number');
pm.expect(r, 'gdo_number').to.have.property('gdo_number');
pm.expect(r.documents, 'documents.address').to.have.property('address');
console.log('Captured dryRunVisitId=' + r.visit_id + '  (' + r.client_code + ' ' + r.client_name + ', service_date ' + r.service_date + ')');
} else { console.warn('No dry-run reports returned.'); }

request.description:
The real live queue of code-27 visits awaiting their online report. Empty (count 0) until launch. A visit stays here until the county confirms its report. Read-only.

--- 2026-08-11: ONE ROW PER (TICKET, PERMIT) ---
A client with N active GDO permits owes Miami-Dade N reports per qualifying dump ticket (we pump both traps). Each row now carries gdo_number for the permit THAT ROW IS FOR, plus a new gdo_id column.
The queue serves at most ONE permit per ticket per batch: the 20h manifest-grained lease holds the rest until the served one is filed. So a multi-permit ticket appears again on a later poll with its next permit, and a three-permit client files over about two days. Nothing about the 25-row cap changes.
You do NOT need to send the permit back. We resolve it server-side from the pair we served.

exec: const j = pm.response.json();
pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('mode = live', () => pm.expect(j.mode).to.eql('live'));
console.log('Live queue count = ' + j.count + '  (0 until launch: only code-27 visits serviced on/after the cutoff appear).');

request.description:
Logs a retryable failure (e.g. portal timeout) for the captured visit. Fresh GUID run_id each send. dry_run:true keeps it out of the live pipeline. Expect 201.

--- 2026-08-11: RESPONSE NOW REPORTS WHETHER THE EVIDENCE LANDED ---
Every 200/201 now also returns:
  screenshot_stored          boolean, true only if the image is actually in the bucket
  screenshot_missing_reason  our drop reason when it is not (SCREENSHOT_TOO_LARGE, SCREENSHOT_DECODE_FAILED, STORE_FAILED), else null
An oversize, undecodable or unstorable image is still recorded as a filing and still answers 201: a real county filing must never be lost over a screenshot problem. You can now SEE the drop instead of having to infer it.
On a deduped 200 these describe the STORED row, not what you just posted, because a dedupe uploads nothing.

gdo_id and gdo_number are ACCEPTED AND IGNORED. You do not need to send them; we resolve the permit ourselves. They are accepted only so a bot built against the earlier draft contract cannot 400 on a filing that already happened.

body.raw:
{
  "visit_id": {{dryRunVisitId}},
  "manifest_id": {{dryRunManifestId}},
  "run_id": "{{$guid}}",
  "status": "ERROR_PORTAL_TIMEOUT",
  "retryable": true,
  "attempted_at": "{{$isoTimestamp}}",
  "failure_reason": "Postman test - portal timed out",
  "screenshot_missing_reason": "no screenshot in test",
  "dry_run": true
}

exec: pm.test('Run "Queue - dry-run" first to capture a visit', function () {
const v = pm.collectionVariables.get('dryRunVisitId');
pm.expect(v, 'dryRunVisitId (run the dry-run queue first)').to.be.a('number');
const j = pm.response.json();
pm.test('recorded (201 new or 200 dedupe)', () => pm.expect([200,201]).to.include(pm.response.code));
pm.test('recorded flag true', () => pm.expect(j.recorded).to.eql(true));
console.log('recorded id=' + j.id + '  deduped=' + j.deduped);
pm.test('screenshot_stored is false when no image was sent', function () {
const r = pm.response.json();
pm.expect(r).to.have.property('screenshot_stored');
pm.expect(r.screenshot_stored).to.eql(false);

item.name: Evidence 1 - result with NO image (sets evidenceRunId)

request.description:
Posts a result with NO screenshot and an explicit screenshot_missing_reason. This is the shape the bot uses when the county confirmation email has not arrived yet: the filing is recorded straight away and the evidence follows.

Run "1. Queue - dry-run" first so dryRunVisitId is captured. This request generates evidenceRunId and the rest of the folder reuses it.

Expect 201 with screenshot_stored:false.

exec: pm.collectionVariables.set('evidenceRunId', 'pm-evidence-' + Date.now().toString(36));
const j = pm.response.json();
pm.test('201 created', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));
pm.test('recorded without evidence', () => {
pm.expect(j.recorded, 'recorded').to.eql(true);
pm.expect(j.screenshot_stored, 'screenshot_stored').to.eql(false);
pm.expect(j.screenshot_missing_reason, 'reason').to.eql('EMAIL_PENDING');
console.log('Result stored with evidence pending, run_id=' + pm.collectionVariables.get('evidenceRunId'));

request.description:
Attaches the evidence to the result posted above. The image here is a 1x1 PNG, deliberately, to show that the stored extension follows the REAL BYTES: the path comes back .png even though the older contract only ever wrote .jpg.

Expect 200 with attached:true, and cleared_missing_reason echoing the EMAIL_PENDING that was on the row.

exec: const j = pm.response.json();
pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('attached, and the reason was cleared', () => {
pm.expect(j.attached, 'attached').to.eql(true);
pm.expect(j.screenshot_stored, 'screenshot_stored').to.eql(true);
pm.expect(j.cleared_missing_reason, 'cleared_missing_reason').to.eql('EMAIL_PENDING');
pm.test('extension follows the bytes (.png)', () => pm.expect(j.screenshot_path).to.match(/\.png$/));

item.name: 5. Monthly LWT report (read-only, no side effects)

request.description:
The Miami-Dade LWT monthly report for the last completed month.

READ ONLY: no lease, no dispense, no side effects. Safe to run as often as you like, unlike the queue.

Returns only IN-SCOPE activities. Scope is evaluated PER ACTIVITY, not per ticket: pickup county = Dade OR the ticket offloaded in Miami-Dade. A ticket with no in-scope activity is omitted entirely, and excluded_rows tells you how many rows that cost so nothing is dropped silently.

Note gallons is ALWAYS null by design: the filed quantity is the truck capacity, resolved from the decal on your side. truck and truck_capacity_gallons are provided.

exec: // Use the last COMPLETED month, which is what a monthly filing is about.
const d = new Date();
d.setUTCDate(1); d.setUTCMonth(d.getUTCMonth() - 1);
const m = d.getUTCFullYear() + '-' + String(d.getUTCMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0');
pm.collectionVariables.set('reportMonth', m);
console.log('reportMonth = ' + m);
const j = pm.response.json();
pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('shaped as expected', () => {
pm.expect(j.month).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('reportMonth'));
pm.expect(j.county).to.eql('Miami-Dade');
pm.expect(j.tickets).to.be.an('array');
const rows = (j.tickets || []).flatMap(t => t.rows || []);
pm.test('every returned row is in scope', () => rows.forEach(r => pm.expect(r.in_scope).to.eql(true)));
pm.test('gallons is always null (resolve from the decal)', () => rows.forEach(r => pm.expect(r.gallons).to.eql(null)));
pm.test("pickup_date is the VISIT date, not the dump date", () => {
// 🛑 THE REGRESSION EVERY DOC NAMES AS THE ONE TO WATCH. Until now this asserted only
// typeof pickup_date === "string", so setting pickup_date := offload_date on every row
// left the entire suite GREEN.
// The discriminator is measured, not guessed. derm_manifests.service_date is a misnomer
// holding the DUMP date and equals dump_ticket_date on 94.5% of live manifests, so if
// pickup_date ever served it, almost every row would EQUAL its offload_date. Live today:
// 92% are STRICTLY BEFORE (grease is pumped before it is dumped). No overlap.
const pd = pm.response.json().tickets.flatMap(t =>
t.rows.map(r => ({ p: r.pickup_date, o: t.offload_date, code: r.client_code })));
pd.forEach(r => pm.expect(r.p, "pickup_date missing on " + r.code).to.be.a("string"));
if (pd.length >= 10) {
const nBefore = pd.filter(r => r.p < r.o).length;
pm.expect(nBefore * 2 > pd.length,
"only " + nBefore + " of " + pd.length + " pickups precede their offload -- " +
"pickup_date looks like it is serving the DUMP date rather than visits.visit_date"
).to.eql(true);
if (pm.response.headers.get('ETag')) { pm.collectionVariables.set('monthlyEtag', pm.response.headers.get('ETag')); }
console.log(j.ticket_count + ' tickets, ' + j.row_count + ' rows, ' + j.excluded_rows + ' excluded');
// Added because the harness was silent on both fields on the day their shape changed.
const _rows = pm.response.json().tickets.flatMap(t => t.rows);
pm.test("state is a USPS two-letter code on every row", () => {
// A value that is NOT two letters is us passing an UNRECOGNISED state through
// verbatim, on purpose, so it is visible rather than silently relabelled to FL.
// If this fails, do NOT print that value on the county form -- report it.
const bad = _rows.filter(r => r.state !== null && !/^[A-Z]{2}$/.test(r.state));
pm.expect(bad.map(r => r.client_code + "=" + JSON.stringify(r.state)),
"unrecognised state passed through").to.eql([]);
// 🛑 AND FL MUST ACTUALLY BE PRESENT. The filter above skips nulls BEFORE testing shape,
// and nothing else asserts a state is ever there -- so setting state := null on all 80
// rows of a live month passed this entire suite. That is the State column printing blank
// on a whole Miami-Dade filing.
// 🛑 A CROSS-FIELD CHECK, because a presence check cannot see a wrong-but-valid state.
//    `some(r => r.state === "FL")` passes if ANY single row is FL, so FL->"GL" on one row,
//    or ->NY on half of them, or on 79 of 80, all passed on every month. The shape check
//    accepts NY, GL and FK alike -- being two capitals is not being RIGHT.
//    County and state are independent fields from the same property, so they must agree:
//    every county we serve is a Florida county (live: Dade 559, Broward 120, Palm Beach 7,
//    plus 14 no-property rows).
//    ⚠ The obvious justification -- "a non-Florida property carries a non-Florida county"
//    -- is NOT true of our data, and the real reason is stronger. Measured: properties
//    154, 396 and 567 are Beverly Hills addresses carrying state=California AND
//    county=Dade. Since the view derives in_scope from county='Dade', one of those taking
//    a pickup would be FILED AS MIAMI-DADE ACTIVITY on the strength of a wrong county.
//    So this check going red on them is a TRUE positive, not a false alarm -- it is the
//    only thing that would notice. (All three have zero visits today, so it is latent.)
//    The genuinely out-of-state rows -- Manhattan Beach, Cedarhurst, the two Levis
//    addresses -- carry county=NULL and are not matched by FL_COUNTIES at all.
const FL_COUNTIES = ["Dade", "Broward", "Palm Beach", "Monroe", "Collier", "Lee",
"Martin", "St. Lucie", "Indian River", "Okeechobee", "Hendry", "Glades"];
const mismatch = _rows.filter(r => FL_COUNTIES.includes(r.county) && r.state !== "FL");
pm.expect(mismatch.map(r => r.client_code + ": county " + r.county + " but state " +
JSON.stringify(r.state)),
"a Florida county is paired with a non-Florida state -- one of the two is wrong, and " +
"both print on the county form").to.eql([]);
pm.expect(_rows.some(r => r.state === "FL"),
"no row carries a state at all. If the addresses are gone too this is a broken " +
"property join; if the addresses are intact the STATE MAPPING itself has failed. " +
"Either way the State column would print blank on the whole filing").to.eql(true);
// 🛑 AND A NULL STATE MUST MEAN "NO PROPERTY AT ALL". Measured on the live view: the null
// crosstab is an EXACT DIAGONAL (measured 2026-08-25; the counts grow, the SHAPE is the invariant) -- 686 rows with none of state/address/city/zip/county
// null, and 14 with ALL FIVE null. No third combination exists. So a null state beside a
// present address is a NEW defect, not the known no-property case.
const halfNull = _rows.filter(r => r.state === null && (r.address !== null || r.city !== null));
pm.expect(halfNull.map(r => r.client_code),
"state went missing on its own, with the address still present").to.eql([]);
// 🛑 THE DIAGONAL IS AN "IFF", AND THE GUARD ABOVE ONLY TESTED ONE DIRECTION.
// Nulling address on every row was caught on 7 of 8 months ONLY by the accent test --
// whose message then blamed the accent fold -- and on 2026-03, which carries no accent
// carrier at all, NOTHING failed. Live the crosstab is exactly two combinations:
// 686 rows with none of state/address/city/zip/county null, and 14 with ALL FIVE null.
// Blank-string is a different shape and is caught by the emptiness check below.
const loc = r => [r.state, r.address, r.city, r.zip, r.county];
const mixed = _rows.filter(r => { const n = loc(r).filter(v => v === null).length;
pm.expect(mixed.map(r => r.client_code + "=" + JSON.stringify(loc(r))),
"a row has SOME location fields null and others populated -- the live shape is all-or-nothing, so this is a new defect, not the known no-property case").to.eql([]);
// ⚠ zip and state were MISSING from this list when it was written, so a blank ZIP on every
//   row of a filing passed all 22 tests on all 8 months -- exactly what the message below
//   says it prevents. Enumerate every location field, not the ones that came to mind.
const blankLoc = _rows.filter(r => [r.address, r.city, r.county, r.zip, r.state].some(
v => typeof v === "string" && !v.trim()));
pm.expect(blankLoc.map(r => r.client_code),
"a location field is an empty string -- it would print blank on the form").to.eql([]);
// zip must look like a zip when present. Live: 0 of 700 malformed.
const oddZip = _rows.filter(r => r.zip !== null && !/^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$/.test(String(r.zip)));
pm.expect(oddZip.map(r => r.client_code + "=" + JSON.stringify(r.zip)),
"a zip is not a 5-digit or ZIP+4 value").to.eql([]);
pm.test("state is never the long form", () => {
pm.expect(_rows.filter(r => r.state === "Florida"), "pre-2026-08-25 long form").to.eql([]);
pm.test("client_name carries no typographic punctuation", () => {
// curly quotes, en/em dash, NBSP. Folded to ASCII at the source.
const bad = _rows.filter(r => junk.test(r.client_name || ""));
pm.expect(bad.map(r => r.client_code), "typographic punctuation").to.eql([]);
pm.test("accented LETTERS are preserved, not stripped", () => {
// Espanola Way and Fendi Chateau are CORRECT spellings of a real street and a real
// business. A run with zero accents where accents are expected is a REGRESSION, not a
// cleaner result -- it means somebody "fixed" the fold into an unaccent().
// The guard names the three codes that ACTUALLY carry an accent, measured against the
// live view: 014-JOY and 179-CIG (448/409 Espanola Way, in address) and 167-FEN (Fendi
// Chateau, in name). An earlier version named 016-FIA/017-FIA -- those are Fialkoff's,
// whose only non-ASCII was the curly apostrophe THIS FOLD REMOVES, so the guard could
// never fire on them and 2026-05 was silently skipped.
const accented = /[\u00C0-\u024F]/;
const carriers = _rows.filter(r => /014-JOY|167-FEN|179-CIG/.test(r.client_code));
// 🛑 SAY HOW MANY WERE CHECKED. The body below sits inside `if (carriers.length)`, so a
// green tick meant EITHER "three carriers verified" OR "nothing was checked at all" --
// and 2026-03 genuinely contains no carrier row, so the silent case is real, not
// hypothetical. Renaming the three codes would have left the suite green having asserted
// nothing.
console.log("accent carriers checked: " + carriers.length +
(carriers.length ? " (" + carriers.map(r => r.client_code).join(",") + ")"
: " -- NOTHING WAS VERIFIED THIS MONTH"));
if (carriers.length) {
// Exact strings, not "contains some accent": a fold that stripped ONE of the two
// accented characters would still satisfy a contains-check.
const EXPECT = { "167-FEN": "Fendi Ch\u00e2teau Residences" };
carriers.forEach(r => {
if (EXPECT[r.client_code]) {
pm.expect(r.client_name, "exact name for " + r.client_code)
.to.eql(EXPECT[r.client_code]);
if (/014-JOY|179-CIG/.test(r.client_code)) {
pm.expect(/Espa\u00f1ola Way/.test(r.address || ""),
"n-tilde stripped from " + r.client_code + ": " + r.address).to.eql(true);
const kept = carriers.filter(r => accented.test((r.client_name||"") + (r.address||"")));
pm.expect(kept.length, "accents were stripped from " +
carriers.map(r=>r.client_code).join(",")).to.eql(carriers.length);
pm.test("rows are returned in the documented total order", () => {
// offload_date, ticket_number, pickup_date, visit_id, manifest_id.
// 🛑 THIS MUST COMPARE SEQUENCE, NOT UNIQUENESS. An earlier version asserted that
// visit_id was unique per row -- true on all 690 rows and true with every .order()
// removed, so it tested nothing. Before 2026-08-25 the sort had 3 keys and 571 of 690
// rows sat in tie groups, so identical calls could differ in sequence.
const j = pm.response.json();
const key = t => [t.offload_date, t.ticket_number];
const tk = j.tickets.map(key);
for (let i = 1; i < tk.length; i++) {
pm.expect(JSON.stringify(tk[i-1]) <= JSON.stringify(tk[i]),
"tickets out of order at " + i + ": " + tk[i-1] + " then " + tk[i]).to.eql(true);
j.tickets.forEach(t => {
const rk = t.rows.map(r => [r.pickup_date, String(r.visit_id).padStart(10,"0")].join("|"));
for (let i = 1; i < rk.length; i++) {
pm.expect(rk[i-1] <= rk[i], "rows out of order in ticket " + t.ticket_number +
" at " + i + ": " + rk[i-1] + " then " + rk[i]).to.eql(true);
// Record the filing size so the include=all request can actually compare against it. Its
// test asserted only row_count >= 1, which cannot fail on any month that returns a row.
pm.collectionVariables.set("monthlyFilingRowCount", String(pm.response.json().row_count));
pm.collectionVariables.set("monthlyFilingExcluded", String(pm.response.json().excluded_rows));
// --- 2026-08-25 iteration 8: three fields nothing was asserting -----------------
pm.test("client_name is present on every row", () => {
// 🛑 Nothing asserted this. Blanking the Business Name column on the whole filing passed
// all ten tests on 6 of 8 months: the punctuation test reads `r.client_name || ""`, so a
// blank is vacuously clean, and the only other reference compares exact names for the
// three ACCENT CARRIERS. On the two months it did fail, the message blamed the accent
// fold for a blank-name defect -- a misleading failure is barely better than none.
// This is the same hole closed for `state`, left open on the sibling field.
// Live: 0 of 700 view rows are null or blank, so there is no false-positive risk.
const blank = _rows.filter(r => !r.client_name || !String(r.client_name).trim());
pm.expect(blank.map(r => r.client_code || "(no code)"),
"client_name blank -- the Business Name column would print empty").to.eql([]);
pm.test("data_quality.checked is true", () => {
// 🛑 The folder contained ZERO references to data_quality, checked, conflicts or anomaly,
// so `checked: false` with conflicts emptied passed every test on every month.
// postman/README.md 4c is explicit that this is the one thing to read before filing:
// checked:false means the CHECK failed, so an empty conflicts list proves nothing.
// Same fail-open family as the null-state blind spot. Live: true on all 8 months.
const dq = pm.response.json().data_quality;
pm.expect(dq, "data_quality block missing entirely").to.not.eql(undefined);
pm.expect(dq.checked,
"data_quality.checked is not true -- the conflict overlay FAILED, so an empty " +
"conflicts list proves nothing. Do NOT file on this payload").to.eql(true);
pm.test("truck_capacity_gallons is a known fleet capacity", () => {
// 🛑 CORRECTED 2026-08-26: this is NOT the filed quantity and NOT the fee basis. Jonathan
// confirmed the county bills MEASURED gallons per manifest from the invoice, and ticket 828837
// is Moises / decal C1184 / capacity 9000 here while the county bills it at 3,800. This test
// is still worth having as an INTERNAL CONSISTENCY check (a truck must report its own
// capacity), but nothing on the county form is computed from it. Do not restore the old
// wording: it would send the next reader to the wrong field. `gallons` is null on 700/700.
// Measured live: Moises 9000, David 1800, Cloggy 126 (Goliath 4800 is decommissioned but
// still appears on historical rows). 6 of 700 rows carry no truck, and those correctly
// carry no capacity -- that is a known gap, not a failure, so it is allowed through.
// 0 rows have a truck with a null capacity, and 0 carry a capacity outside the fleet.
// 🛑 PER-TRUCK, not membership. A membership check let every David row report 9000 with
// NOTHING FAILING on any month. Still a real defect (the value is wrong), but the consequence
// is INTERNAL, not a five-fold county fee. The mapping is strictly 1:1
// live (Moises 9000 n=425, David 1800 n=224, Cloggy 126 n=45, and 0 trucks carry two
// capacities), so naming it costs nothing in false positives.
// Goliath 4800 is decommissioned but may still appear on historical rows.
const CAP = { "Moises": 9000, "David": 1800, "Cloggy": 126, "Goliath": 4800 };
const withTruck = _rows.filter(r => r.truck !== null && r.truck !== undefined);
const badCap = withTruck.filter(r => !FLEET.includes(r.truck_capacity_gallons));
const wrongCap = withTruck.filter(r => CAP[r.truck] !== undefined &&
r.truck_capacity_gallons !== CAP[r.truck]);
pm.expect(wrongCap.map(r => r.truck + " reported " + r.truck_capacity_gallons +
" but is " + CAP[r.truck]),
"a truck is reporting the WRONG capacity for itself, an internal consistency error. " +
"NOTE: this is NOT the filed quantity; the county bills measured gallons").to.eql([]);
pm.expect(badCap.map(r => r.truck + "=" + JSON.stringify(r.truck_capacity_gallons)),
"a truck carries a capacity that is not one of ours, an internal consistency " +
"error, not a filed-quantity error").to.eql([]);
// and a row with no truck must not invent a capacity
const ghost = _rows.filter(r => (r.truck === null || r.truck === undefined) &&
r.truck_capacity_gallons !== null);
pm.expect(ghost.length, "a row with no truck carries a capacity").to.eql(0);
pm.test("ticket_number is present and distinct per ticket", () => {
// 🛑 The manifest identifier PRINTED ON THE COUNTY FORM, and nothing asserted it.
// null / "" / deleted / a uniform "999999" across every ticket all passed every month --
// even the ordering test, whose sort key stays monotonic under a uniform value.
// Live: 0 null and 0 blank of 700 rows, and every ticket object carries its own number.
const t = pm.response.json().tickets;
const bad = t.filter(x => !x.ticket_number || !String(x.ticket_number).trim());
pm.expect(bad.length, "a ticket has no ticket_number -- the Manifest/Ticket # column " +
"would print blank on the filing").to.eql(0);
const nums = t.map(x => x.ticket_number);
pm.expect(new Set(nums).size,
"two tickets share a ticket_number -- a uniform or duplicated identifier makes the " +
"filing unreconcilable against the paper manifests").to.eql(nums.length);
pm.test("the conflicts payload is internally consistent", () => {
// 🛑 Only data_quality.checked was asserted; the payload it guards was not. Emptying
// conflicts, flipping violates_guard to false, or stamping every row with an anomaly all
// survived on every month -- including 2026-07, which carries the live visit 6756 /
// ticket 830673 conflict that README 4c says to check against the paper before filing.
// Product-reachable: index.ts filters conflicts to visit ids shown this month, so a
// join-key regression yields checked:true / count:0 / conflicts:[] -- indistinguishable
// from a genuinely clean month unless the pieces are cross-checked.
const j = pm.response.json();
const dq = j.data_quality;
pm.expect(dq.conflicts.length, "conflict_count disagrees with the conflicts array")
.to.eql(dq.conflict_count);
dq.conflicts.forEach(cf => {
// ⚠ `x === undefined || x === null` PASSES A BLANK STRING, so conflict_kind := "" survived.
//   Check emptiness, not just presence.
["visit_id", "ticket_number", "conflict_kind"].forEach(k =>
pm.expect(cf[k] === undefined || cf[k] === null,
"conflict is missing " + k).to.eql(false));
pm.expect(String(cf.conflict_kind || "").trim() === "",
"conflict_kind is blank -- the reason a row was flagged is the whole point of " +
"reporting it").to.eql(false);
pm.expect(j.tickets.some(t => t.ticket_number === cf.ticket_number),
"a conflict names ticket " + cf.ticket_number + ", which is not in this month's " +
"response -- the conflict and the filing disagree about what was returned")
.to.eql(true);
// every flagged ROW must correspond to a reported conflict, and vice versa
const rowFlagged = j.tickets.flatMap(t => t.rows).filter(r => r.anomaly).map(r => r.visit_id).sort();
const reported = dq.conflicts.map(cf => cf.visit_id).sort();
pm.expect(rowFlagged, "the rows carrying an anomaly do not match data_quality.conflicts -- " +
"one of the two is lying about what was found").to.eql(reported);
pm.test("each row is a distinct activity", () => {
// 🛑 A join fan-out that duplicates every filed row DOUBLES the reported activities and,
// a duplicated manifest line would double its billed gallons too. It passed every test on the
// four months carrying no conflict, and on the other four failed only with a message
// blaming the conflicts payload.
// ⚠ An earlier version of the ordering test asserted visit_id UNIQUENESS and was replaced
// by a SEQUENCE assertion because uniqueness alone tested nothing about order. The right
// answer was BOTH, not either. Live: 700 distinct visit_ids across 700 rows.
const ids = _rows.map(r => r.visit_id);
const dupes = ids.filter((v, i) => ids.indexOf(v) !== i);
pm.expect([...new Set(dupes)],
"the same visit appears on more than one row -- a join fan-out inflates both the " +
"activity count and would duplicate a manifest line").to.eql([]);
pm.test("the response accounting adds up", () => {
// ticket_count and row_count are what a reader trusts without counting. Live they are
// exact; nothing asserted them, so ticket_count := 999 survived every month.
const j = pm.response.json();
pm.expect(j.tickets.length, "ticket_count disagrees with the tickets array")
.to.eql(j.ticket_count);
const rows = j.tickets.reduce((n, t) => n + t.rows.length, 0);
pm.expect(rows, "row_count disagrees with the rows actually returned").to.eql(j.row_count);
const empty = j.tickets.filter(t => t.rows.length === 0);
pm.expect(empty.map(t => t.ticket_number),
"a ticket carries zero rows -- README 4c says a ticket with no in-scope activity is " +
"omitted entirely, so an empty one should not appear").to.eql([]);

item.name: Monthly - include=all (the superset you filter yourself)

request.description:
The same month with NOTHING filtered: every row of every ticket, in-scope or not, each carrying county / pickup_in_dade / in_scope.

Use this if you would rather apply the scope rule yourself. row_count here equals the filing set plus excluded_rows.

exec: const j = pm.response.json();
pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('include flag echoed', () => pm.expect(j.include).to.eql('all'));
pm.test("the superset really is a superset of the filing set", () => {
// Was: pm.expect(j.row_count).to.be.at.least(1) -- unfailable on any month returning a
// row, and it never referenced the filing set at all. The filing request now stores its
// own row_count so this can compare, and the arithmetic below was never asserted anywhere.
const all = pm.response.json().row_count;
const filed = Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("monthlyFilingRowCount"));
const excl  = Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("monthlyFilingExcluded"));
pm.expect(Number.isFinite(filed), "run the filing request first").to.eql(true);
pm.expect(all >= filed,
"include=all (" + all + ") is smaller than the filing set (" + filed + ")").to.eql(true);
pm.expect(filed + excl, "filed + excluded should equal the superset").to.eql(all);
// ⚠ Every guard above degenerates gracefully at equality, so stripping all out-of-scope
// rows AND reporting excluded_rows = 0 satisfies the lot (80 >= 80, 80 + 0 === 80).
// Scope filtering is the entire purpose of this endpoint, so assert it still happens.
// Measured across all 8 months of 2026 (2026-08-25): excluded_rows runs 10..19 and is never 0.
if (all >= 20) {
pm.expect(excl > 0,
"the filing set excluded nothing from a " + all + "-row superset -- either every " +
"pickup really was in Miami-Dade, or the scope filter has stopped filtering"
).to.eql(true);
const rows = (j.tickets || []).flatMap(t => t.rows || []);
pm.test('carries out-of-scope rows too', () => pm.expect(rows.some(r => r.in_scope === false) || j.excluded_rows === 0).to.eql(true));

request.description:
Send the ETag from the first request back as If-None-Match. A repeated poll for an unchanged month costs a 304 with no body.

Run "Monthly - filing set" first so monthlyEtag is captured.

exec: pm.request.headers.add({ key: 'If-None-Match', value: pm.collectionVariables.get('monthlyEtag') || '' });
pm.test('304 Not Modified', () => pm.response.to.have.status(304));

request.description: Month must be YYYY-MM with a real month number. Expect 400 month_required_yyyy_mm.

exec: pm.test('400', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
pm.test('names the reason', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('month_required_yyyy_mm'));
